title: Deterministic mockserver scenarios and VCR contract validation for SDK streaming + retry ergonomics
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a deterministic mockserver and VCR-friendly contract test suite across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs focused on streaming ergonomics and retry/backoff semantics. Goal: eliminate flakiness in CI by encoding realistic Redwood API behaviors (partial responses, connection resets, delayed tokens, intermittent 5xxs) as replayable fixtures and assert that each SDK's streaming client recovers, emits consistent events, and preserves message order and idempotency guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible set of 10 deterministic scenarios implemented as mockserver routes (see scenarios list)
A VCR-style recorder and playback mode for unit tests that produces stable fixtures checked into repo

End-to-end contract tests in each SDK that validate: reconnect + resume semantics, exponential backoff + jitter config, streaming chunk ordering, and correct error propagation to user callbacks/promises
CI runs use playback mode by default; record mode gated behind an env var and approved PRs
Documentation and example snippets added to sdk/README for how to run record/playback and how to extend scenarios
At least one flaky test class eliminated from the SDK monorepo (tracked in QA board)
scenarios: partial-kv-cache-hit: server sends initial tokens then pauses mid-token before resuming after 150ms
intermittent-5xxs: streaming connection returns 502 on first frame then succeeds on reconnect
reset-during-batch: TCP reset after 2nd token; client should resume with cached prefix and no duplication
late-function-call: function-calling event emitted after final token (ensure callbacks run in order)
slow-heartbeat: keepalive frames delayed beyond client threshold to force heartbeat reconnect path
long-tail-tokens: single response with thousands of tiny token frames to test buffering limits
auth-refresh-during-stream: token expires mid-stream; client must fetch refresh token and continue
backpressure-burst: rapid-fire requests causing temporary 429s and a fallback to serialized mode
binary-attachment-frame: attach binary chunk in middle of stream to test binary-safe streaming APIs
vcr-mismatch: subtle header ordering / header case differences to validate recording normalisation
implementation_notes: Mockserver: extend existing sdk-test-mockserver (github.com/redwood-inference/mockserver) with deterministic timing controller and RNG seed param
Recording: use VCR-like fixture format (yaml/ndjson) capturing headers, frames, and timing deltas; add an explicit seed field to make replay deterministic
SDK bindings: expose `PlaybackMode::Record` and `PlaybackMode::Replay` in all three SDKs with identical env var toggles (REDWOOD_SDK_REC_MODE)
Retry semantics: canonicalize exponential backoff (base=100ms, factor=2, jitter=full) and expose as config object; tests validate 3 retry attempts by default
Streaming ergonomics: standardize event types across SDKs - 'token', 'error', 'done', 'reconnect', 'resume' - and assert order in contract tests
Test harness: CI will mount fixtures and run with mocked network disabled; separate pipeline job for 'record' runs on nightly infra with real Redwood staging service
Flakiness mitigation: normalise timestamps and random IDs in fixtures with placeholders replaced at playback time

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Recording live sessions could capture PII or secrets. Mitigation: recorder redacts Authorization, cookies, and any header matching /token/i; add manual allowlist for additional fields.
Risk: Behavior drift between playback and live server. Mitigation: schedule nightly 'record' pipeline against staging with alerts on diff regression.
Risk: SDK API surface changes across languages leading to divergent behavior. Mitigation: maintain single conformance test matrix and require green contract tests for SDK releases.
